scope: RELAY persistence, cancellation and concurrent edits
ECHO provenance, access revocation and invalidation

initial.note: Captured before implementation fixes. The export finding has three failing variants; live cancellation has two.

final.note: All original regressions and the additional allowlisted-ancestor symlink check pass. Initial failures and the partially fixed stage are retained.

findings.title: Allowlisted paths can follow symlinks into excluded source trees
findings.reproduction: In an isolated synthetic tree, place a sample file under private/ and link to it from src/linked.txt, src/linked-dir, or README.md; call export into a new review directory.
findings.observed_before_fix: All three variants copied the excluded sample and returned PREPARED_FOR_REVIEW with audit PASS. Directory and root-file variants scanned zero files.
findings.expected: Reject symlinks or reject resolved sources outside explicitly permitted trees before copying any content.
findings.impact: The directory allowlist does not enforce the documented exclusion of private imports. This is a concrete review-copy leak path; no real private data was used or exported.
findings.quality_claim_affected: README says the review copy excludes private imports and runtime databases.
findings.resolution: Selected source paths and every ancestor component are checked for symlinks by both the privacy scanner and exporter; no output directory is created for rejected sources.

findings.title: Uncited cached retrieval content survives source access revocation
findings.reproduction: Cache the primary-color query, change the uncited identity source in the same Atlas instance to require partner access, confirm scoped evidence lookup denies it, then repeat the exact query.
findings.observed_before_fix: The exact cache hit still contained the identity source text in retrieval.context and retrieval.required, with its old public permission metadata.
findings.expected: Revalidate or remove every source-bearing field returned in the cached response, including retrieval payloads.
findings.impact: The complete response violates the current source access decision even while cited claims remain permitted. Reproduction requires an in-process source permission change; a rebuilt Atlas changes the corpus namespace.
findings.quality_claim_affected: SECURITY says cache admission and hits revalidate exact source claims and source previews enforce scope; returned ancillary source text was unchecked.

findings.title: Cache validation does not close the set of claims over dependencies
findings.reproduction: Extend a persisted answer with a genuine clearspace quote and matching claim, without adding its evidence ID to answer.evidence_ids or the dependency hashes; request the cached query again.
findings.observed_before_fix: The altered answer was accepted as an exact hit.
findings.expected: The sets of claim evidence IDs, declared evidence IDs and dependency keys must agree.
findings.impact: Corrupted or malformed persisted answers can bypass complete provenance validation. The test mutates temporary cache state; this is not proof of a remote cache-write primitive.
findings.quality_claim_affected: Complete source provenance for cached emitted claims.

findings.title: Invalidation for one brand evicts valid entries in another namespace
findings.reproduction: Cache identical queries for luma and veyra, then invalidate with luma scope while both sources remain unchanged.
findings.observed_before_fix: The veyra entry was removed because it was checked using luma permissions and brand.
findings.expected: Scope-local invalidation only checks matching namespaces and preserves unrelated valid entries.
findings.impact: Unrelated cache work is discarded, causing avoidable recomputation and incorrect invalidation accounting; no cross-scope disclosure was demonstrated.

findings.title: An active workflow silently drops a different submitted edit
findings.reproduction: Pause the first resume at search after accepting First text, issue a second resume with Second text, then release the first worker.
findings.observed_before_fix: The second resume returned normally; the final brief and artifact package contained First text.
findings.expected: Persist the newly accepted edit or return an explicit conflict. Identical duplicate submissions may reuse the active operation.
findings.impact: Concurrent user edits are lost without an error, potentially causing review of an obsolete brief.
findings.quality_claim_affected: Durable continuation and concurrent resume behavior.

findings.title: Live bookkeeping overwrites a concurrently committed cancellation
findings.reproduction: Commit cancel while a fake provider is pending and then fail the provider; separately commit cancel after the draft tool returns but before usage is persisted.
findings.observed_before_fix: The first path changed cancelled to failed; the second restored awaiting_approval from a stale checkpoint.
findings.expected: Persist usage and failure details through guarded transactions that retain the current terminal state.
findings.impact: Cancellation is not stable in the opt-in live adapter, despite fixture workers correctly fencing artifact commits. No real provider was contacted.

tests.name: test_public_export_rejects_link_in_allowlisted_parent
tests.initial_note: Added after the first implementation retest; the corresponding ad hoc reproduction failed at the partial-fix stage.

passed_controls: Fixture cancellation during search prevents artifacts and ledger effects.
All five RELAY HTTP state/artifact/mutation operations deny a run owned by another principal.
limitations: Small authored adversarial suite, not a complete security audit or production authentication certification.
Source mutation and persisted-answer corruption are deliberately injected into temporary synthetic state.
Fake-provider contract tests do not establish live model quality, cost, latency or reliability.
No actual private source, credential, external account or provider was accessed.
Passing regression tests after fixes would establish only the exercised boundaries.

followup_checks.name: symlink_in_allowlisted_ancestor
followup_checks.reproduction: Create private/public-demo/sample.txt in a temporary synthetic project and point datasets to private using a directory symlink. The selected datasets/public-demo path itself and its descendants are ordinary paths.
followup_checks.observed: The revised exporter copied the excluded sample into review/datasets/public-demo/sample.txt.
followup_checks.expected: Reject symlinks in any ancestor component of the selected source path as well as the selected source and descendants.
followup_checks.method: Isolated ad hoc reproduction after inspecting the implementation fix; original 11-test file unchanged.
followup_checks.final_observed: privacy_check returns FAIL; export raises ValueError and leaves no review-copy directory.
